title: Trace a word on a letter board
prompt:
Return true if word can be spelled on board, a grid of lowercase letters, by starting on any cell and stepping up, down, left or right without using a cell twice.

- board is a list of equal-length lowercase strings with 1 to 12 rows and 1 to 12 columns.
- 1 <= word.length <= 15, lowercase.
- Return a boolean.
hints: Try every cell as a starting point for word[0], then extend the path one neighbour at a time.
Use depth-first search with backtracking: mark a cell as in use before exploring from it and unmark it when you return.
Abandon a branch as soon as the next letter does not match. A quick precheck that the board has enough copies of each letter in word rules out many impossible words immediately.

solution.explanation: Depth-first search from each cell follows only neighbours matching the next letter. Temporarily overwriting the current cell with "#" marks it as used on this path, and restoring it on return lets other paths use it. The letter-count precheck rejects words the board cannot possibly contain before any search starts.

complexity.notes: L is the word length. After the first step each cell has at most 3 unused neighbours to try. Space covers the mutable board copy and recursion depth L.

followUps: You must check thousands of words against the same board. How would a trie of the words help?
